wikiGoal:
A knowledge wiki for the Kissaten coffee bean discovery platform. This wiki covers three overlapping areas:

1. **Code & Architecture** — Concise quickstart, architecture overview, source map, key workflows, operations/runbook notes, testing guidance, and integration points. Inspect git history to understand reasoning behind code changes. Keep pages grounded in the repository structure and recent code changes. Prefer practical navigation for engineers over generic summaries.

2. **Coffee Domain Concepts** — Document the specialty coffee knowledge that underpins this database: coffee processing methods (washed, natural, honey, anaerobic), varieties (Bourbon, Gesha, Catuai, etc.), origin geography (countries, regions, elevations, the coffee belt), roast levels and profiles, cupping scores, tasting note taxonomy, price transparency fields (FOB, farm gate price), and decaffeination. Explain why the data model captures each field and how the domain concept maps to schema fields in BEAN_DATA_FORMAT.md and the Pydantic models. These pages help future contributors understand not just how the code works but why specific coffee attributes are modeled the way they are.

3. **Design & UX Concepts** — Document the product design decisions that make this coffee database useful: the guided discovery experience (explore by flavour, process, or varietal), faceted filtering system, the interactive origin map, bean detail page information architecture, roaster/origin exploration flows, and the analytics/insights dashboards. Explain how each design pattern helps users discover and compare coffee, and reference the frontend components and API endpoints that implement them.

When documenting, link between these three areas: a coffee domain concept should point to the schema fields and UI that implement it; a design pattern should reference the domain concepts it surfaces and the components that render it; a code page should reference the domain concepts it operates on. The goal is a wiki that helps both engineers and coffee-savvy contributors understand the system end to end.

pages.purpose: FastAPI endpoints and DuckDB layer; add the /v1/roasted-in/{slug} location-detail endpoint and document the requires_review / include_unreviewed public-search contract.
instructions: Add an endpoint group for roaster-location exploration: GET /v1/roasted-in/{slug} (src/kissaten/api/main.py around line 3316) resolves a country or region slug from roaster_location_codes, matches roasters hierarchically via the scraper registry, and returns statistics, top roasters, top origins, varietals, and cities; it is cached with a SimpleMemoryCache.

Document the review-flag search contract: public search/list endpoints hide rows with requires_review=true via REVIEW_HIDDEN_SQL unless include_unreviewed=true (admin); an explicit requires_review filter is a hard filter (the admin queue uses requires_review=true); is_tasting_kit is a hard filter like is_decaf. pages.title: Accounts, Beta & Admin Console
pages.purpose: User accounts and community systems: better-auth magic-link auth, user roles and beta flags, profile settings, the admin console (stats, user management, beta approval, roaster suggestions triage, flagged-for-review queue), and the roaster suggestion lifecycle with voter notifications.
instructions: Admin console (admin/+page.svelte): stats (getAdminStats), searchable user list, beta-interest approval/decline, roaster suggestion tabs (pending/approved/rejected/implemented) with reject and implement dialogs — the implement dialog validates the chosen slug against live catalogue roasters (data.allRoasters from the layout) before marking implemented.
Admin gating: the requireAdmin() pattern in server commands/queries (401/403) plus the +page.server.ts role check that redirects to /login and raises a friendly 403 rendered by +error.svelte.

Auth: better-auth with magicLink + emailOTP plugins on the Drizzle SQLite adapter; custom /login/verify URL carries token and callback params; an in-memory otpStore hands the OTP to the email sender; databaseHooks.user.create.after fires notifyAdminNewSignUp. Document the user table fields: role (user|admin, migration 0009), isBetaAllowed / betaEnabled / betaInterest (0008), newsletterSubscribed, defaultRoasterLocations.
Profile (profile.remote.ts): name, newsletter, beta enable/interest toggles, default roaster locations; admin notifications on beta request and newsletter change.

Roaster suggestions (roaster_suggestions.remote.ts): auth-required submit (name + normalised name, country, website; 'exists' result on duplicate), upvote with notifyOnImplementation consent flag, public list ordered by upvotes; implemented suggestions disappear from the list because the real roaster (from DuckDB) takes their place. Document the status lifecycle pending → approved/rejected → implemented with a Mermaid diagram, and the email fan-out (submitter digest + opted-in voters + admin digest) via markSuggestionImplemented — cross-link frontend/email-notifications.md.

pages.title: Page Feedback System
pages.purpose: End-to-end user feedback system: FeedbackContext built by page load functions, the dialog with its three modes and honeypot, the submitFeedback server command, the page_feedback SQLite table, admin email digests, and how feedback rows are resolved back to source bean JSON.

Client side: shared dialog open-state store (feedbackDialog.svelte.ts) so the floating button in the (main) layout and inline triggers (FeedbackInlineTrigger) open one instance; dialog modes undecided → data-wrong / comment / not-a-bean; field picker grouped by section with per-field suggested-value inputs (typed: text/number/textarea/month/select/tags via FeedbackFieldInput); the dialog resets on open and auto-closes when the URL changes; the `website` field is a honeypot (Zod max(0) rejects bots with 400).

Field builders: frontend/src/lib/utils/beanFeedback.ts (getBeanFeedbackFields) maps a CoffeeBean into display values (price, weight, in_stock, cupping_score, tasting notes, elevation, coordinates, variety) truncated to ~60 chars, grouped into 'Bean details', 'Pricing & stock', etc.
Include a Mermaid lifecycle diagram (dialog → submitFeedback → page_feedback → admin email → apply-review-decisions / manual JSON fix). See /skills/mermaid-diagrams/SKILL.md.

Server side (frontend/src/lib/api/feedback.remote.ts): submitFeedback is auth-optional, captures reporter user/email/UA/IP, inserts a page_feedback row (id fbk_<nanoid>, status 'new'), and fires notifyAdminPageFeedback with a formatted fields summary.

Validation rules from frontend/src/lib/schema/feedback.ts: free-text message only required when no fields selected and kind ≠ not-a-bean (min 20 chars); fields capped at 50, values at 8000 chars.

pages.purpose: The guided tasting experience: wizard state machine and SCA-style flavour taxonomy, Dexie persistence, the tasting history route hierarchy with breadcrumbs and custom-bean namespace disambiguation, session list/summary cards, and PNG image export with its native-share gesture constraints.
instructions: Custom namespace disambiguation: under /tasting/history/custom/<slug>, the page decides between single-bean mode and roaster-group mode by checking whether the slug matches a beanUrlPath or a custom bean syncId (see [bean_slug]/+page.svelte refresh() logic); custom roaster names are slugified via slugifyCustomRoaster/getCustomRoasterName in tasting_utils.ts.

History routes: /tasting/history lists sessions grouped into month buckets (frontend/src/lib/utils/history.ts groupSessionsByMonth, tested in history.test.ts); nested routes [roaster_slug], [roaster_slug]/[bean_slug], .../[tasting_id] resolve names from the loaded sessions + roasters API for breadcrumbs (+layout.svelte).

Image export: tasting_utils.ts copyTastingAsImage + imageGenerator.ts — native navigator.share with files requires the blob to be already cached (awaiting generation consumes the user gesture on mobile), so share-on-first-tap only happens when cached; otherwise it falls back to clipboard (ClipboardItem) or download with a toast prompting a second tap. Document this constraint explicitly — it is easy to break.
Mention TastingSummaryCard/TastingSessionList/ListItem components and the noindex robots meta on history pages.
Use British English; use a Mermaid diagram for the route hierarchy or wizard steps (see /skills/mermaid-diagrams/SKILL.md).

Wizard: TastingWizard.svelte step machine (basics → overview → category → mouthfeel → summary) built on Svelte 5 runes; flavour taxonomy and defect notes live in frontend/src/lib/tasting/ (see docs/GUIDED_TASTING_PLAN.md); sessions are saved to Dexie (localdb) with $state.snapshot to strip reactive proxies, then synced (cross-link frontend/sync-system.md).

pages.title: wait0 SSR Cache Proxy
pages.purpose: The wait0 cache-first SSR reverse proxy (wait0.yml): where it sits between nginx and the Bun origin, its per-route caching rules and cache-key design, auth-path bypasses, warmup and URL persistence, and the invalidation API used after scrape/refresh/promote cycles.
instructions: Document the deployment position: nginx → wait0 (:8080, RAM 100m + LevelDB disk 1g) → Bun SSR origin (127.0.0.1:3000), serving stale-while-revalidate with a 10m expiration.

Explain each rule block from wait0.yml: (1) never cache /auth, /admin, /vault, /profile, /login, /tasting (per-user/personal data); (2) /search and /flavours must vary by the full list of high-cardinality query params (q, smart_query, all facet filters, page/per_page/sort) or every search would share one cache entry; (3) paginated catalog pages (/processes, /varietals, /roasters) vary only by page/sort params; (4) /brew-assistant varies by bean_url_path; (5) catch-all for path-only pages where unlisted query params (utm_*) never fragment the cache. All cacheable rules bypass when better-auth session cookies or the kissaten-currency cookie are present.
Include a Mermaid request-flow diagram. Use British English.

Invalidation API: POST /wait0/invalidate authenticated by WAIT0_API_AUTH_TOKEN (scopes invalidation:write / stats:read); this is how a path/tag is purged after a scrape/refresh/promote cycle — tie it into the operations promotion flow (refresh → cp → restart → invalidate).
Note the debug headers (X-Wait0-*) for diagnosing cache misses.
Warmup: catalogue URLs discovered from the sitemap index; urlPersister remembers successfully cached URLs across restarts (data/urls.yaml, flushed every 30s, forgetAfterFailures 3).
